original_question: Which gene is defective in patients with glycogen storage disease type Ib, which is caused by a deficiency in glucose-6-phosphate translocase?
key_entities: glycogen storage disease type Ib, which is caused by a deficiency

final_qi.question: Which gene is defective in patients with glycogen storage disease type Ib, which is caused by a deficiency in glucose-6-phosphate translocase?
final_qi.long_answer: Glycogen storage disease type Ib results from loss-of-function mutations in the SLC37A4 gene, which encodes the microsomal glucose-6-phosphate translocase (G6PT). Defective SLC37A4 prevents transport of glucose-6-phosphate into the endoplasmic reticulum for hydrolysis, leading to the metabolic abnormalities characteristic of GSD Ib.

final_answer.long_answer: Glycogen storage disease type Ib is caused by loss-of-function mutations in the SLC37A4 gene, which encodes the endoplasmic-reticulum glucose-6-phosphate translocase (G6PT). Defective SLC37A4 prevents transport of glucose-6-phosphate into the ER lumen, blocking its hydrolysis by glucose-6-phosphatase and producing the metabolic and hematologic manifestations characteristic of GSD Ib.
